setup: Use large plates so you can roll under
Pad the bar, set it over your hip crease
Lie back, knees bent, feet flat
Hold the bar just outside your hips
execution: Drive your hips up through your heels
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top
Lower until the plates touch lightly
faults: Don't arch your lower back to finish
Don't bounce the plates off the floor

notes: Use full-size plates so the bar sits high enough to slide under, and a thick pad across the hips.
The range is short; the top should be a glute squeeze with ribs down, not a back arch.
To get out, lower the bar to the floor and roll it down your thighs, or sit up and lift it off.
Log the bar and plates together (total).
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, knees bent, feet flat about hip-width, hips on the floor. Bar on a pad across the hip crease, hands holding it.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Hips raised so the body is straight from shoulders to knees; upper back and shoulders still on the floor. Ribs down, glutes squeezed.

ikHints: Shoulders and feet fixed on the floor
Bar stays on the hip crease
emphasise: Hips rise to a straight line from shoulders to knees
Ribs stay down at the top
